granularity_detail: Only an indirect proxy (Universal Thermal Climate Index, UTCI) at 0.25 degree grid - no dedicated heat-stress index exists.

Dedicated "extreme heat" indices (Hot Days, Tropical Nights, Warmest 3-day Period, Climatological/Apparent Temperature Heatwave Days) at 0.25 degree grid (~28km), directly downloadable via the ECDE indicator dataset.
Dedicated Fire Weather Index and High Fire Danger Days indices at 0.1 degree grid (~11km), based on the same EFFIS classification, directly downloadable via the ECDE indicator dataset.
Dedicated "severe windstorm" index (Extreme Wind Speed Days) at 0.25 degree grid (~28km), directly downloadable via the ECDE indicator dataset.
Only an indirect proxy (Aridity Actual index) at 5km grid - no dedicated water-stress index exists.
Dedicated river-flood indices (Flood Recurrence, River Discharge) at 5km grid, directly downloadable via the ECDE indicator dataset.

Dedicated "extreme precipitation" indices (Maximum Consecutive 5-Day Precipitation, Extreme Precipitation Total/Days) at 0.25 degree grid (~28km), directly downloadable via the ECDE indicator dataset.
Dedicated meteorological drought indices (SPI-3 Duration/Magnitude) at 0.25 degree grid, plus a soil-moisture drought index at 5km grid, directly downloadable via the ECDE indicator dataset.
Not covered: no distinct heat-stress index or category exists in either module (Heat wave loss data is a different, event-based metric).

UTCI is a complex multi-variable derived index (temperature, humidity, wind, radiation); no ready-made version exists among the raw CDS variables - see copernicus_climate_indicators for the standalone ERA5-HEAT product.
Raw ERA5 soil-temperature-at-depth variables could serve as model input for permafrost analysis, but no ready-made permafrost index or product exists.

Dedicated "extreme heat" indices (tropical nights, hot days, heatwave days) exist as part of the sis-ecde-climate-indicators dataset on the CDS, but are not a prominently findable feature of Copernicus CDS as a general-purpose entry point - practically accessed via Climate-ADAPT rather than by browsing CDS directly.

Fire Weather Index requires a specific multi-variable fire-danger model, not derivable from raw meteorological variables alone - see copernicus_climate_indicators for the standalone CEMS Fire Danger product.

Derived "severe wind storm" index exists as part of the sis-ecde-climate-indicators dataset on the CDS, but is not a prominently findable feature of Copernicus CDS as a general-purpose entry point - practically accessed via Climate-ADAPT rather than by browsing CDS directly. Raw 10m wind-speed ERA5 variables remain available for custom modelling.
Aridity requires evapotranspiration modelling, not derivable from raw meteorological variables alone - see copernicus_climate_indicators for the standalone SMHI hydrology product.
River discharge/flood recurrence requires hydrological modelling, not derivable from raw meteorological variables alone - see copernicus_climate_indicators for the standalone SMHI hydrology product.

Derived heavy-precipitation indices exist as part of the sis-ecde-climate-indicators dataset on the CDS, but are not a prominently findable feature of Copernicus CDS as a general-purpose entry point - practically accessed via Climate-ADAPT rather than by browsing CDS directly. Raw precipitation ERA5 variables remain available for custom modelling.

Meteorological drought (SPI-3) is derivable from raw precipitation variables with moderate own processing; the soil-moisture drought component requires hydrological modelling - see copernicus_climate_indicators for the standalone SMHI hydrology product covering that component directly.
No GLOF-relevant dataset or index identified on the CDS.
No ready-made erosion index exists; would require independent erosion modelling (e.g. RUSLE-type) from raw precipitation intensity, soil moisture and wind-speed variables.
No landslide-relevant dataset or index identified on the CDS.
